answer: Under the rule, every agent identity must name an operator, and any violation by one identity freezes all that operator's identities and charges the operator a fixed 0.03 ETH cleanup fee per identity, never the wallet. That fee is collected even when the wallet is empty, so an attacker spreading identities across a dune of addresses pays the same operator charge for each one. A gale of cheap wallets cannot dodge it, because the yarrow in the operator's ledger marks the cleanup bill that scales with every identity.
